How Often Do Puppies Poop and Pee? By Age and Dog Size

Puppies usually poop 3 to 5 times a day and pee far more often than that. How much and how often they eat matters more than their size, and once they're adults, 1 to 2 poops a day is common for dogs of any size.

Daily potty count by age (common guidelines)

AgePoops per dayHow long they can hold pee
2–3 monthsAbout 4 to 5. They often go after every meal.About 2 to 4 hours
4–6 monthsAbout 3 to 4About 4 to 6 hours
7–12 monthsAbout 2 to 3Gradually getting closer to an adult.
Adult1 to 2 (up to 3)Give them a chance at least once every 6 to 8 hours

A common rule of thumb is that puppies can hold their pee for "their age in months + 1 hour." At 3 months, that's about 4 hours. But this is closer to a maximum than a target, so taking a puppy out more often than that also helps with potty training. Adult guidelines are in how often a dog should poop and potty intervals.

When puppies usually need to go

  • Right after waking up
  • 10 to 30 minutes after eating
  • Right after an exciting play session
  • After drinking a lot of water

Take them to their potty spot at these moments and praise them when they go. Potty training goes much faster.

Potty count by dog size

SizePoopPeeNotes
Small dogs1 to 2 a day is common.Small bladders, so they tend to go more often.Small amounts make soft stools and diarrhea easy to miss. Dehydration also sets in quickly.
Medium dogs1 to 2 a day is common.AverageVaries a lot with activity level.
Large dogs1 to 2 a day is common.A lot at once.They eat more, so they poop more.

Rather than size changing the count dramatically, how much they eat, how many meals they get, and how active they are matter more. That's why knowing your own dog's usual count matters more than an average. If your dog only goes on walks, also see how to track potty for a dog who only goes outside.

When to worry

  • See a vet now: a puppy with both diarrhea and vomiting (hurry even more if they haven't finished their vaccinations), bloody stool, or a limp, listless puppy
  • See a vet now: straining to pee with nothing coming out
  • Talk to your vet: no poop for more than a day, or a sudden big rise or drop in how often they pee
  • Talk to your vet: poop firmness or color that's been off for several days. Check it with the dog poop color and firmness chart.
This article is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems low on energy or has symptoms that worry you, talk to your vet.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many times a day do puppies poop?

Usually about 3 to 5 times a day, more often than adult dogs. They eat more meals and digest quickly, so they often go soon after eating.

How many hours can a puppy hold their pee?

A common rule is "their age in months + 1 hour." At 3 months that's about 4 hours, but it's closer to a maximum, so take them out more often.

Do small dogs go more often than large dogs?

Poop count depends more on how much and how often they eat than on size, so most adult dogs go 1 to 2 times a day. Small dogs do tend to pee more often.

My puppy hasn't pooped all day.

They may be eating less, or their surroundings may have changed. If they strain and seem uncomfortable, or are vomiting or losing their appetite, talk to your vet.
